justifications.c1: Independent prosecution figures tied to fencing failures: RJ McLeod £800,000 for failing to adequately inspect and maintain perimeter fencing (COPFS, search-confirmed), £600,000 (insufficient fencing) and £20,000 (partial fencing); theft costs are vendor aggregates (BauWatch, ProFM), and there is no £ figure for blown-over or unclipped panels.
justifications.c2: Wind-related fencing failures are noted (Building Safety Group, Morgan Sindall SHE alert title, AU and NZ regulators) and ~6,000 site thefts a year (2014), but no per-site incident rate and no sourced daily walk-round duty; the costed events are rare child-injury cases.
justifications.c3: Workarounds are CDM steps per HSG151, hirer call-outs to re-stand panels (US) and hired alarm or camera towers (unpriced); no labour cost for perimeter walks or patrols was found.
justifications.c4: CDM 2015 reg 13(4)(b) requires steps to prevent unauthorised access (legislation.gov.uk), with enforcement in this niche (RJ McLeod £800k for not inspecting and maintaining fencing, search-confirmed; £600k CDM case), and an AXA CAR10 endorsement excluding overnight plant theft unless in a fully enclosed yard (FOS DRN-5658159, search-confirmed).
justifications.c5: No job advert or budget owner was found (site manager, project manager or security subcontractor), and panel hire at £3.50–£10.90 a week caps what a per-panel device can cost.
justifications.c6: National hire networks (National Tool Hire Shops, Lakeside, Mammoth, SafeSite) already deliver fencing to these sites, and security firms (BCM Security with Reconeyez) sell site monitoring, but no hirer is shown selling fence monitoring and maintenance-visit evidence was not found.
justifications.c7: HERMEQ Pulse temporary fencing already detects panel movement, cuts and climbing (search-confirmed) and CCTV and alarm towers hold larger sites; nothing is priced, and the rentable clip-on sensor gap is evidenced only by absence.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN tilt/vibration nodes ($49.99 Codepoint CS1040) and $5 BLE modules exist, but a ~£40 sensor equals 5–8 weeks of panel hire, forcing sparse placement that may miss a single unclipped panel; a gateway is also needed.
justifications.c9: The CDM duty runs for the whole construction phase and fence hire is billed weekly, so rental fits, but no comparable fence-sensor subscription price was found and there is no record-retention duty.
justifications.c10: Prosecutor and regulator enforcement (COPFS, HSE cases), trade press (SHP, Construction Index, BSG), a tier-1 contractor SHE alert and an ombudsman decision on an unfenced site's theft claim; no first-hand forum complaints about blown-over fencing.

weakest: The costed incidents are rare catastrophic prosecutions with no per-site frequency, and per-panel economics (£3.50–£10.90 weekly hire) leave little room for a sensor on each panel.
